flashcards.q: To find the K largest elements, do you use a min-heap or max-heap of size K, and why?
flashcards.a: Min-heap of size K — its root is the weakest member of the current top-K set, exactly what a new candidate must beat and what gets evicted.

flashcards.q: What is the time and space complexity of the size-K heap approach to top-K?
flashcards.a: O(n log k) time, O(k) space — beats O(n log n) full sort whenever k << n.

flashcards.q: What is QuickSelect's average and worst-case time complexity, and why the gap?
flashcards.a: Average O(n) via T(n)=T(n/2)+O(n) since you recurse into only one side; worst O(n^2) if the pivot is always min/max (e.g. sorted input with a fixed pivot), fixed by randomizing the pivot.

flashcards.q: How do you solve Top-K Frequent Elements in O(n) without a heap?
flashcards.a: Bucket sort: allocate n+1 buckets indexed by frequency (bounded by array length), place each distinct value in its bucket, read top-down until k collected.

flashcards.q: K Closest Points to Origin — what heap key should you use and why?
flashcards.a: Squared Euclidean distance (x^2+y^2) in a max-heap of size k — sqrt is unnecessary since it's order-preserving (monotonic).

flashcards.q: Running median of a stream — what structure and why?
flashcards.a: Two heaps: max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper half, rebalanced to keep sizes within one of each other; median is top of larger heap or average of both tops.

flashcards.q: At true internet scale (unbounded keys, distributed), why does an exact top-k heap stop working, and what replaces it?
flashcards.a: Per-key exact counting doesn't fit in memory or across machines; approximate sketches (Count-Min Sketch, Space-Saving algorithm) bound memory at the cost of a small, bounded overcount error.
